solve: Re-solved by T-1881 (2026-11-07) to the photograph alone, the image store's 1024 x 809 px copy of LC-D4-12552 (det 4a08066, c. 1900), in the house's footprint frame (u 0 at the rear wall, rising west to the Prairie front at 27.75; v 0 at the north wall, rising south to the 18th Street flank at 17.93). The print looks west-north-west at the house's south-east corner from Calumet Avenue south of 18th Street: the flank's east section lit, the rear (east) face in shade, the low east range and the stable to the right. READ OFF THE PRINT, and checked against the GLB's own vertices (the K01 walls, the bays and the porte-cochere): the main block's south-east corner, a sharp lit/shade edge at x 393 with the cornice's top at y 352 (u 0, v 17.93, 12.9 m); the rear face's north end at x 545, its cornice at y 367 (the rear pavilion p_rear's face, u -0.9, v 0); the rear step's return at x 458 (u -0.9, v 11.48, where p_rear ends); the 18th Street pavilion's (bays.p_18th) east return, the dark banded strip at x 326-342 between the lit east section and the lit pavilion face (u 7.15, v 17.93 at x 342 and v 19.23 at x 326); the porte-cochere's east end, its deck's balustrade running from the block's outer corner at x 241 (u 13.05, v 23.9) back to the pavilion at x 288 (v 19.23), its top at y 425 (7.9 m). FITTED (level, principal x at the centre): least squares over those seven plan points and three heights, 2.4-2.6 px rms, every residual under 6 px (the deck's top the largest). THE EYE'S HEIGHT: the house alone does not fix it (an eye at 1.6 m and one at 6.5 m fit the same points to within 0.3 px rms, trading height against distance and focal length), so it is taken from the street: the gas lamp at x 146-165, 140 px from its foot (y 563) to its finial (y 423), puts the horizon about 1.6 m over its foot at y 488-495 for a lamp of 3.0-3.3 m, and the 18th Street coping's piers, which stand about 1.8 m, show their tops nearly level across the print (y 491-496); the 1.6 m fit's horizon is y 491.9. With the eye at 1.6 m: u -70.52, v 77.64, heading 136.32 degrees, focal 1118.7 px, horizon y 491.9. That stands the photographer on Calumet Avenue's east side about 30 m south of 18th Street, looking north-west across the crossing, as the print's foreground shows: the corner's curb sweeping round at the right and 18th Street's curb running away to the left; at about 90 m and a focal length of 1119 px (a 49 degree field) where the earlier solve needed 479 px (94 degrees). WHAT IT REPLACES: the earlier solve (eye u -39.79, v 36.62, 3.79 m; heading 129.23; focal 478.8; horizon 454.5) was fitted to the rear face, the deck's cresting, the porte-cochere's deck and the stable's corner; it fitted the rear face as well as this one but drew the whole 18th Street flank foreshortened, the pavilion's return 19-22 px and the porte-cochere 40 px right of the print's (20.6 px rms over the points above), which the match record had read as the porte-cochere standing 4 m out of place. CHECKS NOT IN THE FIT: the rear face's window heads render at x 420, 483 and 523 (the print's 422, 477, 522) and its dormers at 422, 486 and 523 (427, 476, 524); the step's stack at x 494-514 (494-509); the flank's triple at x 295-316 (299-317) and its broad ground-storey windows at 297-315 and 347-367 (297-316, 349-372). WHAT IT DOES NOT FIT, written into the match record: the main block reads about 10 % taller in the print than built (the mansard's deck edge and cresting about 10 px, 0.8 m, over the render's at the corner), as Taylor's no. 1445 reads the flank; and the stable at the right edge, which the earlier solve used as a fit point, now falls about 135 px left of the print's corner building (another structure's place, judged in its own record). UNCERTAINTY: about 0.1 m a pixel along the flank's east section and 0.3 m a pixel in depth there; the eye's height is the street's, and the house's grade is taken as the street's. LIGHT: the flank lit and the rear face in shade, so the sun stands in the south-west (sun_uvy, the companion print's). SEASON: the elms are bare but for a few last leaves and the ivy on the house still holds its leaves, so the review's trees stay in winter and the ivy is drawn in leaf.
